dataChanges.description: Populate existing ownerActor and ownerSession fields from the allocating caller instead of synthesizing session identity from ticket and timestamp; preserve existing lease schema and historical records.

architecture.decision: Preserve the existing allocator and change-lease schema. Add explicit actor/session inputs to allocation and a shared read-only writer check in the existing lease verifier, synchronized to its bundled copy. Hooks resolve the canonical primary checkout and validate the lease for the actual affected branch, comparing caller identity and fencing without deriving identity from the lease itself. Run the check before successful hook exits for ticket branches and for each ticket ref received on pre-push stdin. Reuse existing lease diagnostics and document accepted handoff requirements; hooks neither renew leases nor approve handoffs. Local inspection found no active registered ticket or competing worktree; historical leases are preserved and do not establish takeover authority. Re-observe ownership before implementation.
interfaceChanges: Allocator accepts explicit writer actor and session identity.
Lease verifier exposes a read-only writer-check command with explicit operation and ref bindings.
Ticket-branch hooks require matching caller identity and current fencing evidence.
architecture.rollback: Revert the bounded implementation through the governed delivery process; preserve all existing worktrees, leases and receipts, and require explicit ownership reconciliation before resuming affected branches.

nonGoals: Create a new allocator, repository, controller service or runtime dependency.
Modify external controllers, coordinate with other repositories or acquire credentials.
Migrate adoption contracts, rewrite existing leases or automatically reclaim expired ownership.
Replace protected review and merge authority with local hook results.
Provide protection against a malicious operating-system user who can modify hooks or impersonate process environment.
Allocate tickets, edit files, commit or publish during this planning request.
delivery.outcome: Bind ticket allocation and local Git mutation checks to the same explicit writer session, rejecting cross-session amendments and pushes while retaining existing canonical worktree allocation.

validation.evidence: Allocation fixtures verify exact caller identity and fail-before-effect behavior for absent or invalid identity.
Real Git fixtures exercise both hook variants: owner commit/amend succeeds and a second session is rejected without changing HEAD.
Local bare-remote fixtures verify owner and non-owner pushes, forced updates, multiple refs and pushes from another checkout; rejected pushes leave remote refs unchanged.

Negative fixtures cover invalid identity, stale fencing, unsafe lease paths, expiry, release, publication freeze and untrusted handoff evidence; accepted successor fixtures bind independently supplied controller evidence.
Compare primary checkout status and file bytes before and after successful and refused allocations, including allocation invoked from a linked checkout.
Record regression and governance results against the implementation HEAD; verify bundled verifier parity and retain independent publication approval requirements.

summary: Close issue #495's remaining writer-fencing gap while preserving the allocator's existing canonical worktree creation and clean-primary behavior.
